title: Occupancy and Residency Certification: Annual Certification Calendar Schedule
content:
The annual calendar of the Occupancy and Residency Certification profile is set by the figures below. Each figure is a property of the certification plan the profile is held under; this schedule lists every plan.

## Calendar figures common to all plans

The following figures are identical under each of the six plans (Standard Annual Certification, Joint Borrower Certification, Non-Borrowing Spouse Household Certification, Deferral Period Certification, Living Trust Certification and Authorized Representative Certification).

| Calendar figure | Value under every plan |
|---|---|
| Interval between annual occupancy certifications | 12 calendar months |
| How each annual due date is set | on the anniversary of the loan's closing date |
| Certification request mailed | 30 calendar days before the due date |
| Earliest signature that counts for the cycle | 60 calendar days before the due date |
| Email reminder, where an email address is on file | 14 calendar days before the due date |
| Second notice, if the certification is incomplete | 10 calendar days after the due date |
| Final notice, if the certification is incomplete | 25 calendar days after the due date |
| Response grace period, after which an incomplete certification makes the profile overdue | 30 calendar days after the due date |
| Certification year assigned to a cycle | the calendar year of the cycle's due date |

## Request channels by plan

| Plan | Channels the certification request is sent through |
|---|---|
| Standard Annual Certification | mail and email |
| Joint Borrower Certification | mail and email |
| Non-Borrowing Spouse Household Certification | mail and email |
| Deferral Period Certification | mail and email |
| Living Trust Certification | mail only |
| Authorized Representative Certification | mail only |

## Reading the schedule

Every figure counted in days is counted in calendar days from the cycle's due date, before it or after it as the table states. The certification year is never the year of mailing or of signature: a cycle whose due date falls in a given calendar year carries that calendar year as its certification year.

**Hypothetical illustration (generic dates, not a customer record).** Take a profile under any plan whose due date is a hypothetical 1 June. The request is mailed on 2 May, 30 days earlier, and where an email address is on file the email reminder falls on 18 May, 14 days before the due date. A signature dated 2 April, 60 days before the due date, is the earliest that counts for that cycle; one dated 1 April is too early. If the cycle is still incomplete, the second notice falls on 11 June and the final notice on 26 June. The cycle's certification year is the year in which that 1 June falls. Under Living Trust Certification or Authorized Representative Certification the same request is sent through the mail channel only.

## Questions the schedule answers

- *Does every plan run on a twelve-month cycle?* Yes; the interval is 12 calendar months under all six plans, and each due date is a closing anniversary.
- *Which plans receive the request by email as well as by mail?* Standard Annual, Joint Borrower, Non-Borrowing Spouse Household and Deferral Period Certification; Living Trust and Authorized Representative Certification receive it by mail only.
